subject: inline labels for standard inputs - how to make my package work together with shiny and CRAN

messages.author: 3bf225a8a5f5becd
messages.subject: inline labels for standard inputs - how to make my package work together with shiny and CRAN
parts:
Hi all,

I have a (small) package where I re-implement some of the basic inputs of shiny in such a way that the labels appear on the left and the input on the right. For this, I "hack" into shiny using ::: to have access to functions like choicesWithNames, firstChoice, selectizeIt and so forth. Obviously this prevents my own package from being cran-worthy. Hence I have 3 possible approaches:

- copy all these functions literally into my package (I can't import non-exported objects)
- fork Shiny, export the functions I need, add some help pages for them and hope my fork gets pulled into shiny.
- fork Shiny, add my selectInline, textInline, numericInline etc functions, and hope my fork gets pulled into shiny.
- fork Shiny, add an "inline" option to all the standard input functions, and hope my fork gets pulled into shiny.

My questions:

1. Which method would you pick?

2. I'd love it when I can just add what I need to shiny, but I haven't been able to find somebody who could tell me which option fits best into the underlying design choices made by the shiny dev team.

Cheers
Joris

messages.author: 11c9f8eed87b3505
messages.subject: Re: inline labels for standard inputs - how to make my package work together with shiny and CRAN
parts:
Hello Joris,

To avoid the ::: hack do as Yihui does here: https://github.com/rstudio/DT/blob/ea15ab901b533b64c9f871c182de42117a309b6a/R/shiny.R#L295

So in your package you would do:

choicesWithNames <- getFromNamespace("choicesWithNames","shiny")

Hope that helps. Should be CRAN friendly since DT is on CRAN and does this.

Kind Regards,
Carl
